title: optimize: tune NCCL collectives and KV-cache overlap for tensor-parallel multi-GPU
author: Miguel Rivera
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads were periodically losing overlap between NCCL collectives and device compute when KV-cache continuous batching and async kernels were active, which reduced throughput and increased p99 token latency. This PR makes a targeted set of runtime changes to improve overlap and stability without changing public APIs. Changes include: 1) NCCL stream prioritization and explicit stream affinity for TP collectives to ensure collectives use a dedicated high-priority comm stream while kernels execute on a compute stream; 2) a lightweight collective scheduler that sequences smaller all-reduce/all-gather ops to reduce blocking on large collectives and permit opportunistic kernel launches; 3) adaptive comm/compute synchronization points driven by observed kernel durations and per-batch sequence lengths so we avoid unnecessary device-wide synchronizations; 4) KV-cache continuous-batching integration: allow KV-cache flush/merge operations to run on a background stream and add a fast-path that reorders kv-cache transfers when the comm stream is idle; 5) microkernel hints for fused attention backward and rotary kernels to reduce kernel launch latency when interleaved with collectives; 6) additional metrics and traces (tp.collective_wait_ms, tp.kv_overlap_ratio) and a small benchmark harness used to validate improvements. Benchmark summary: on an 8xA100 TP4 setup running production sequence length mix, steady-state throughput improved by +18% and p99 token latency reduced by 12% across our standard chat workload. Approach: keep kernel/comm changes behind a runtime flag (TP_NCCL_OVERLAP=true) and default to conservative behavior. Rollout plan: enable flag for canary fleet, measure metrics for 72h, then gradual ramp. Backwards compatibility: no API change. Risk: potential rare ordering regressions on non-NVIDIA NCCL-like drivers; guarded with runtime checks and fallbacks. See linked Linear tickets for perf numbers and validation plan.

review_comments: Priya Nair: Great work on isolating the comm path. A few comments: can you add a fallback for drivers that don't support stream priorities? Also please add a unit test for the scheduler when collectives are nested.
Miguel Rivera: Added driver capability checks and a software fallback that serializes on a dedicated host-side stream. Added nested-collective unit test in the latest commit.

Ethan Kim: The adaptive heuristic is promising but we should make the thresholds configurable via env vars for faster experimentation during canary. Also please ensure the KV-cache background transfers respect memory pressure signals.
Miguel Rivera: Exposed TP_NCCL_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD and TP_KVCACHE_BG_MAX_BYTES as env vars. KV-cache transfer now stales out if memory pressure > 80% and falls back to foreground transfer.
Sofia Patel: Bench numbers look solid. Could you add a short note in the rollout doc about rollback conditions and alert thresholds?
Miguel Rivera: Added rollback and alert thresholds to docs/rfcs/2026-02-nccl-overlap.md. Marking as ready for merge once CI passes.

CI: Initial Linux-GPU integration job failed on unit test 'collective_scheduler_nested_test' due to race in test harness. Miguel pushed a fix that adds deterministic ordering to the harness. Rerun results: all checks green.
release_notes: runtime: improve tensor-parallel multi-GPU perf by tuning NCCL stream priorities, scheduling collectives for better overlap with compute, and integrating KV-cache continuous-batching with background transfers. Expect ~18% throughput gain and lower p99 latency on TP workloads. Rollout behind runtime flag and documented in RFC.
